blocks.x: Another year, another ranking from our Readers’ Choice Awards that says the best time to visit Japan is now—the Land of the Rising Sun has once again been voted number one on our list of the best countries in the world. There’s so much to enjoy here, from relaxing ryokans in Kyoto and mesmerizing museums in Tokyo, to the contemporary art installations in the Setouchi Islands and the culinary craft of fermentation in the Niigata prefecture. But when to do it?

Here to offer their advice on the best time to visit Japan, as well as some counsel for first-time visitors, are Condé Nast Traveler Top Travel Specialists who focus on trips to Japan: Andres Zuleta, founder of Boutique Japan, and Alys Colayera of Black Tomato.

The first tip? Accept that you won’t be able to do everything you want to do in a single go. “Japan rewards thoughtful planning, but it’s best not to try to see too much in one trip,” says Colayera. “Allow time to enjoy each place rather than packing in a new city every day, and book sought-after hotels and experiences well in advance during peak seasons.” Just remember, this beautiful archipelagic country is made up of over 14,000 islands—that’s just 14,000 reasons to come back in the future.

So whether you want to put together a wide-ranging grand tour of Japan’s off-the-beaten-path destinations or a perfect weekend in Tokyo, per pop star Rina Sawayama, here’s the best time to visit Japan.

When is the best time to go to Japan?

Winter is the best time to visit Japan for an all-purpose trip. The brisk weather is perfect for enjoying the warmth of hot springs, and views of Mount Fuji are typically better in this season when the air is expected to be clearer. Zuleta of Boutique Japan recommends going after the New Year’s rush: “From around January 15 to March 15, you can almost feel as if you have the country to yourself. The exception is at winter resorts, which will be crowded with skiers and snowboarders.” Just be sure to avoid the winter holidays themselves, when there are significant closures—many shops, restaurants, and other places of interest close for several days or longer around this time of year.

However, as with most destinations anywhere in the world, there are good reasons to go to Japan, regardless of season. When you should go depends on what you’re looking for. In the spring, you of course have cherry blossom season—a gorgeous, yet crowded and expensive time of year. Colayera of Black Tomato suggests setting realistic expectations: “Cherry blossom season is lovely and indeed beautiful, but it is absolutely heaving with people given its popularity and demand. Additionally, it is the most expensive time to be in Japan.” She recommends visiting in the autumn, when the equally-gorgeous changing leaves draw travelers to a lesser extent.

It’s also a fabulous idea to visit Japan in the autumn, when comfortable temperatures and fall foliage arrive.
